I'm considering how to write a JUnit4 test for RecordTypeBuilder without Mockito available in the classpath, so I'll need to either build manual mocks or use the actual JSTypeRegistry, JSType, and Node classes from the rhino package.

Since this is Defects4J Closure-165b, the target class lives in com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype, and since these classes are part of the same source tree rather than an external jar, I can reference them directly. I'll need to check the JSTypeRegistry constructor signature for this version to instantiate it properly, likely passing a TestErrorReporter.

I'm confirming the constructor takes an ErrorReporter, so I'll implement an anonymous ErrorReporter for safety, use registry.getNativeType to grab a real JSType like NUMBER_TYPE, and construct a Node via its public constructor with a Token constant for testing.

Now I'm sketching out the test cases: adding a new property returns non-null and non-empty, adding a duplicate returns null, building with no properties matches the native OBJECT_TYPE, building with properties yields a distinct RecordType instance, and adding a property with a null type doesn't throw since the source has no null check.

Then testing null propertyNode, empty string names, and null names -- since HashMap handles null keys fine, addProperty(null,...) should work the first time and return null on the second (duplicate) call. I want to use real Node and JSType objects from the registry rather than mocks to avoid over-mocking.

I need to make sure the test compiles against the actual Closure classes -- RecordType, JSTypeRegistry, JSType, JSTypeNative, Node, and ErrorReporter -- checking the correct import paths and the ErrorReporter interface's method signatures for warning and error.

I'm implementing an anonymous ErrorReporter that throws on error and ignores warnings, and constructing a Node with Token.NAME for the test setup.

Still writing test class...

Adding more test cases...

I'm asserting the result isn't the same as the native object type, then adding another test to verify that adding a duplicate property still keeps isEmpty false.

Now I'm adding a test to verify that calling addProperty with a null type doesn't throw an exception, since the source code doesn't validate null types.

I'm also adding cases for null propertyNode and empty string property names, confirming addProperty still returns the builder itself in each scenario.

Adding a test case for null property names, checking that HashMap allows null keys so adding twice returns null on the second call.

I'm also adding tests that verify build() returns consistent, cached results when called multiple times on an empty builder, and starting a test for adding multiple distinct properties.

I'm checking whether JSTypeRegistry's constructor actually accepts an ErrorReporter in this older Closure Compiler version, recalling that it likely had two constructor variants around that era.

For RecordType, since its constructor is package-private, I realize the test doesn't need to invoke it directly anyway—checking `instanceof` works regardless of access modifiers as long as the class itself is visible, so package placement isn't actually a blocker here.

RecordTypeBuilder is public with a public addProperty method, and JSTypeRegistry's getNativeObjectType and getNativeType methods should also be public, so I'm set to pull everything together into the final summary.
